briefing.opening: Good morning. I will begin the climate briefing for November 2, 2026.

sections.title: 🔴 Deepening Climate Crisis and Widespread Domestic and International Damages
sections.content: Domestically, cultural heritage and ecosystems face direct threats, with the termite damage risk index for wooden cultural properties rising by 27% due to climate change, and the decline of pine trees accelerating [1, 5]. Internationally, a national emergency was declared in Bolivia due to El Niño-induced drought, affecting over 110,000 households [10, 11], and Pacific island residents warn they are on the brink of ruin [56]. The increase in premature births in Asia and steep temperature rises in some U.S. states demonstrate the widespread impacts of climate change [60, 62], with calls also made for the World Health Organization (WHO) to declare climate change a public health emergency [65]. Notably, the Lancet report predicts Bangladesh will suffer $17.5 billion in income losses by 2025 due to climate change, and scientists' warnings of potential permanent damage to the cryosphere if the Paris Agreement's 1.5-degree target is exceeded further underscore the severity of the current situation [66, 68].

sections.title: 🌱 Domestic Efforts Towards Carbon Neutrality and Renewable Energy Transition
sections.content: Positive movements towards carbon neutrality are active across various local governments and institutions in Korea. Gyeryong City achieved the top ranking in South Chungcheong Province for public sector greenhouse gas reduction performance for two consecutive years [12, 33, 36], and Siheung City was re-designated as an 'Environmental Education City,' promoting accelerated carbon neutrality in conjunction with Lake Sihwa [17, 22, 26]. The Incheon Institute emphasized expanding citizen participation and strengthening incentives for achieving carbon neutrality [14, 15, 16, 25, 28, 30, 34], while cities like Uiwang and Asan encouraged citizens to practice carbon neutrality through walking events and forest experience days [18, 21, 27, 29, 31]. Furthermore, carbon neutrality practices are being implemented in various sectors, including the Korea Forest Service's efforts to secure carbon credits through overseas forest conservation [13] and the upcycling activities of Asan City's Kumyeoul Youth Volunteer Group [23]. The Korean Food Promotion Institute also conducted a carbon-neutral loofah sharing volunteer service [35]. The government, through President Lee's remarks, announced it would accelerate renewable energy expansion, including the creation of 'Sunshine Income Villages' [39, 40, 45, 46, 49]. Corporations are also participating, with Korea Southern Power strengthening its renewable energy development capabilities and KAI promoting increased use of renewable energy [37, 41]. Adaptation efforts also continue, with an increasing number of farms using plant lighting to cope with climate change [3], the search for healthy housing technology companies [8], and the reorganization of agricultural infrastructure [9]. The expansion of renewable energy is acting as a positive signal both domestically and internationally, with K-green companies entering the Australian renewable energy market [38] and environmental groups welcoming Hyundai Steel's completion of solar power generation facilities [42, 50]. AI technology and Germany's sustainable forestry also contribute to climate change response [58, 61].

sections.title: ⚠️ Challenges in Climate Action and Policy Dilemmas
sections.content: Many challenges still exist in responding to the climate crisis. It has been pointed out that the climate crisis cannot be averted by the goodwill of individual nations alone [4], and Jeju Island faces a 'carbon neutrality dilemma' where the increase in electric vehicle registrations leads to tax revenue losses [32]. Internationally, a regressive phenomenon has been observed in India, where despite an increase in renewable energy, coal power generation reached its highest level in three years, leading to a rise in the proportion of fossil fuels [43]. Domestically, conflicts are also emerging in the policy implementation process, such as calls for the withdrawal of the Korea Rural Community Corporation's designation as a mandatory renewable energy supplier [48]. Furthermore, the economic phenomenon where inflation and job issues are prioritized over climate change among Gen Z voters suggests the importance of social consensus for climate action [64]. The Australian Coalition's radical approach to climate change leaves room for political debate [69].

sections.title: 🌍 Global Climate Governance and Awareness Promotion
sections.content: International governance and awareness-raising efforts to address climate change are also ongoing. Corporate accountability is emphasized as an essential element in the era of climate change [59], and as COP31 approaches, strong warnings are emerging that climate change threatens humanity [63]. Domestically, regional-level strategy development continues, with the Gimhae Research Institute hosting an energy economy forum to discuss response strategies for Gimhae's manufacturing industry in the era of climate change [7]. The Prime Minister is chairing the National Climate Change Committee's Supreme Council meeting, leading high-level discussions [67].

briefing.closing: Today's briefing highlighted the severity of the climate crisis, various domestic and international efforts to overcome it, and the challenges that still persist. At this juncture, everyone's attention and action are more crucial than ever for a sustainable future. This concludes the climate briefing for November 2, 2026.
